newsitem.title: USA: Heart disorder often misdiagnosed as "panic attack".
newsitem.headline: Heart disorder often misdiagnosed as "panic attack".

text.p: A curable, recurrent rapid heart rhythm can produce symptoms similar to those of a "panic attack," causing physicians to misdiagnose the condition, according to an article in the March 10 issue of the American Medical Association's publication.
An AMA release said the findings to appear in the Archives of Internal Medicine were based on studies of 107 patients referred for a special heart procedure known as electrophysiologic testing.

Timothy Lessmeier M.D., of Heart Clinics Northwest, Spokane, Wash., and his colleagues found these patients suffered from a non-threatening disorder known as paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT).
"Symptoms due to PSVT frequently fulfil the formal psychiatric criteria for panic disorder," the release said.
Of the study group, about twice as many women as men were misdiagnosed. Also, 12 percent of all patients who were misdiagnosed sought mental health treatment before learning they suffered from PSVT.
In the misdiagnosis, physicians often attributed the PSVT symptoms to panic, anxiety or stress.
Once identified, PSVT patients can receive therapy and may be cured, the release said.

PSVT causes a rapid heartbeat, typically 150-250 beats per minute, that often stops on its own after several seconds or minutes. The researchers report the disorder was incorrectly diagnosed for 55 percent (59) of the patients during initial medical evaluations.
